subject: Payments POC — KMS options, timeline, and immediate asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Singh <a.singh@bluewavepayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Payments POC — KMS options, timeline, and immediate asks

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand the constraint set for the pilot. Quick recap below and three immediate asks so our security/infra teams can scope the POC correctly.

Recap (high level)
- Scope: 3 endpoints for transaction enrichment (payment routing, chargeback analysis, tokenization metadata). No raw card PANs stored in any logs.
- Residency: primary US region (us-west-2) for processing; storage residency required for backups tied to your PCI charter.
- Retention: event payloads persisted for 30 days in readable form for debugging; aggregated metrics retained 13 months.
- Logging: audit trail required for model inputs + request headers (redacted for PII); access logs must be exportable to your SIEM.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.3 required; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (BYOK) preferred — HSM-backed key custody is a strong plus.

Immediate asks (actionable)
1) Can you confirm which key custody model you prefer for the POC: (A) BlueWave-managed KMS (Cloud provider KMS), (B) Customer-managed KMS with us holding only encrypted key references, or (C) On-prem HSM (requires additional deployment step)? Please reply with A/B/C.
2) Please attach your standard KMS/HSM requirements checklist (or the minimal control list) so we can map to Redwood options.
3) Can you share the desired timeline window for the pilot (start date and expected duration)? We need to check Dedicated pool availability for reserved capacity.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short mapping doc (redwood_kms_options_summary.pdf) and a template spreadsheet (bluewave_poc_key_requirements.xlsx) to collect the specifics.

Next steps from our side:
- Marcus will draft a minimal runbook for BYOK flow and what telemetry we will send to your SIEM (sample fields).
- Soojin will pull the compliance checklist and estimate the additional prep work/time for HSM integration.

If convenient, let’s schedule a focused 30-min follow-up early next week to align on the selection so we don’t block procurement.

Thanks —

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Payments POC — KMS options, timeline, and immediate asks

Thanks, Irene — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: we lean toward (B) customer-managed KMS hosted in our cloud account (we want control over key rotation and the ability to revoke). HSM-on-prem (C) is possible but will push timeline by several weeks.

Two follow-ups:
- I’ll share our minimal KMS control spreadsheet (we host a checklist in our security drive) — attaching that shortly.
- For logging: we don’t want full payloads in plaintext in logs. We expect Redwood to redact PAN-equivalents and persist a deterministic token/ID for traceability. Can you confirm how redaction vs tokenization is handled in your runtime?

Proposed timeline: start of pilot week of June 21, run for 4 weeks. Does that work on your end?

Thanks,
Aisha
Director, Product (Payments)
BlueWave Payments

Hi Aisha — thanks for the steer, (B) is the cleanest path for a pilot and matches how we typically run customer-managed keys for short evaluations. A few technical notes and commitments so your security team can evaluate:

Technical notes- BYOK model (customer-managed KMS in your account): we support importing a symmetric key or granting Redwood a key-encrypting-key (KEK) role so we can encrypt model artifacts and at-rest blobs. Keys stay in your KMS; Redwood only stores encrypted references.
- Key rotation: we can honor your rotation cadence; when a key rotates we re-wrap active artifacts and keep an auditable rotation log.
- HSM requirement implications: if you require PKCS11-backed HSM for signing certs or offline key backup, we will need an additional deployment step and a short security review (estimated +2–3 weeks).
- Redaction/tokenization: Redwood can apply deterministic tokenization at ingestion (token stored alongside the redacted payload). We will not retain raw PAN-equivalents in logs. For debugging, we can provide a re-identification workflow that requires an access request and dual-authorization audit trail.

Committed deliverables for pilot
1) Sample KMS integration runbook (audio+doc)
2) SIEM mapping for audit logs (CSV)
3) Short test harness for verification of tokenization vs redaction

Irene / Soojin: I’ve attached a short mapping doc for their security team and a proposed checklist for the re-identification approval flow.

Marcus Lin
Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
